   128→def _is_auth_expired_error(e: BaseException) -> bool:
   129→    """Return True if the exception is or was caused by credential refresh failure.
   130→
   131→    Checks the exception and its __cause__ chain so gRPC-wrapped RefreshErrors
   132→    are detected. Used to avoid retries and to raise AuthExpiredError for the outbox.
   133→    """
   134→    try:
   135→        from google.auth.exceptions import RefreshError
   136→    except ImportError:
   137→        return False
   138→    exc: BaseException | None = e
   139→    while exc is not None:
   140→        if isinstance(exc, RefreshError):
   141→            return True
   142→        exc = getattr(exc, "__cause__", None)
   143→    return False
   144→
   145→
   146→def _categorize_pipeline_error(e: Exception) -> str:
   147→    """Convert exception to human-readable pipeline error reason.
   148→
   149→    Combines extraction and grounding error categorization from both
   150→    the old extraction_service and grounding_service triggers.
   151→
   152→    Args:
   153→        e: The exception that occurred during pipeline execution.
   154→
   155→    Returns:
   156→        Human-readable error message for the user.
   157→    """
   158→    error_str = str(e).lower()
   159→
   160→    # PDF / extraction errors
   161→    if "pdf" in error_str or "pymupdf" in error_str:
   162→        return "PDF text quality too low or file corrupted"
   163→    if "gcs" in error_str or "storage" in error_str or "bucket" in error_str:
   164→        return "File storage service unavailable"
   165→
   166→    # Auth / credential errors (do not retry — trigger login in UI)
   167→    if "credential" in error_str or "auth" in error_str or "refresherror" in error_str:
   168→        return "Google credentials expired — sign in again"
   169→
   170→    # UMLS / grounding errors
   171→    if "mcp" in error_str or "subprocess" in error_str:
   172→        return "UMLS grounding service unavailable"
   173→    if "concept_linking" in error_str or "concept_search" in error_str:
   174→        return "UMLS terminology service unavailable"
   175→
   176→    # Generic transient errors
   177→    if "circuit" in error_str:
   178→        return "AI service temporarily unavailable"
   179→    if "timeout" in error_str or "timed out" in error_str:
   180→        return "Processing timed out"
   181→    if "parse" in error_str:
   182→        return "Protocol parsing failed"
   183→
   184→    return f"Pipeline failed: {type(e).__name__}"
   185→
   186→
   187→def _update_protocol_failed(
   188→    protocol_id: str,
   189→    reason: str,
   190→    error_category: str,
   191→    exception_type: str,
   192→) -> None:
   193→    """Update protocol status to extraction_failed with error metadata.
   194→
   195→    Args:
   196→        protocol_id: Protocol ID to update.
   197→        reason: Human-readable error reason.
   198→        error_category: Short category string for the error type.
   199→        exception_type: Python exception class name.
   200→    """
   201→    try:
   202→        with Session(engine) as session:
   203→            protocol = session.get(Protocol, protocol_id)
   204→            if protocol:
   205→                protocol.status = "extraction_failed"
   206→                protocol.error_reason = reason
   207→                protocol.metadata_ = {
   208→                    **protocol.metadata_,
   209→                    "error": {
   210→                        "category": error_category,
   211→                        "reason": reason,
   212→                        "exception_type": exception_type,
   213→                    },
   214→                }
   215→                session.add(protocol)
   216→                session.commit()
   217→    except Exception:
   218→        logger.exception(
   219→            "Failed to update protocol %s status to extraction_failed",
   220→            protocol_id,
   221→        )
   222→
   223→
   224→async def _run_pipeline(
   225→    initial_state: dict[str, Any],
   226→    config: dict[str, Any],
   227→    payload: dict[str, Any],
   228→) -> dict[str, Any]:
   229→    """Run the pipeline graph with MLflow tracing inside the async context.
   230→
   231→    MLflow ContextVars must be created in the same async context as the
   232→    LangGraph invocation. asyncio.run() creates an isolated context, so
   233→    we initialize MLflow tracing HERE (inside asyncio.run) rather than
   234→    in the sync caller.
   235→
   236→    Each pipeline node creates its own separate MLflow trace tagged with
   237→    protocol_id and run_id, so traces appear in the MLflow UI as they
   238→    complete rather than waiting for the entire pipeline. Filter by the
   239→    run_id tag to see all traces from a single pipeline invocation.
   240→    """
   241→    from protocol_processor.graph import get_graph
   242→    from protocol_processor.tracing import set_pipeline_run_id
   243→
   244→    graph = await get_graph()
   245→
   246→    # MLflow tracing: do NOT enable langchain.autolog() here.
   247→    # Autolog wraps the entire ainvoke() in a single trace that only
   248→    # appears in MLflow after the full pipeline completes.  Instead,
   249→    # each node creates its own independent trace via pipeline_span()
   250→    # so traces appear in real-time as nodes finish.
   251→    # MLflow for this thread is set by handle_protocol_uploaded() via
   252→    # _ensure_mlflow() (protocol-processing-YYYYMMDD). Do not call
   253→    # _ensure_mlflow() again here.
   254→
   255→    # Set run_id so every node's pipeline_span() tags its trace with the
   256→    # same identifier.  Uses the thread_id which is "{protocol_id}:{uuid4}".
   257→    thread_id = config.get("configurable", {}).get("thread_id", "")
   258→    if thread_id:
   259→        set_pipeline_run_id(thread_id)
   260→
   261→    return await graph.ainvoke(initial_state, config)
   262→
   263→
   264→def handle_protocol_uploaded(payload: dict[str, Any]) -> None:
   265→    """Handle a ProtocolUploaded event by running the full pipeline.
   266→
   267→    Constructs the initial PipelineState from the event payload and
   268→    invokes the consolidated 5-node LangGraph workflow via asyncio.run().
   269→
   270→    Uses protocol_id as the LangGraph thread_id so that retry_from_checkpoint
   271→    can locate the saved checkpoint by protocol_id alone.
   272→
   273→    Replaces both extraction_service.trigger.handle_protocol_uploaded and
   274→    grounding_service.trigger.handle_criteria_extracted from the v1.x
   275→    two-service architecture.
   276→
   277→    Args:
   278→        payload: Event payload dict containing protocol_id, file_uri, and title.
   279→
   280→    Raises:
   281→        Exception: Re-raised after logging to let the outbox processor
   282→            mark the event as failed for retry.
   283→    """
   284→    # Set MLflow experiment for this worker thread (protocol-processing-YYYYMMDD).
   285→    # Without this, the thread would use default experiment ID 0, which may be deleted.
   286→    _ensure_mlflow()
   287→    # So pipeline spans carry the experiment ID and export works from any thread.
   288→    try:
   289→        import mlflow
   290→
   291→        from protocol_processor.tracing import set_pipeline_experiment_id
   292→
   293→        exp = mlflow.get_experiment_by_name(_get_experiment_name())
   294→        if exp:
   295→            set_pipeline_experiment_id(exp.experiment_id)
   296→        else:
   297→            set_pipeline_experiment_id(None)
   298→    except Exception:
   299→        logger.debug("Could not set pipeline experiment ID for tracing", exc_info=True)
   300→
   301→    protocol_id = payload.get("protocol_id", "unknown")
   302→    logger.info(
   303→        "Handling ProtocolUploaded event for protocol %s (consolidated pipeline)",
   304→        protocol_id,
   305→    )
   306→
   307→    try:
   308→        # Generate unique thread_id per pipeline run to prevent checkpoint collision
   309→        # on re-extraction (same protocol_id would resume old completed checkpoint)
   310→        thread_id = f"{protocol_id}:{uuid4()}"
   311→
   312→        initial_state: dict[str, Any] = {
   313→            "protocol_id": payload["protocol_id"],
   314→            "file_uri": payload["file_uri"],
   315→            "title": payload["title"],
   316→            "batch_id": None,
   317→            "pdf_bytes": None,
   318→            "extraction_json": None,
   319→            "entities_json": None,
   320→            "grounded_entities_json": None,
   321→            "archived_reviewed_criteria": payload.get("archived_reviewed_criteria"),
   322→            "status": "processing",
   323→            "error": None,
   324→            "errors": [],
   325→        }
   326→
   327→        # Store thread_id in protocol metadata for retry_from_checkpoint lookup
   328→        try:
   329→            with Session(engine) as session:
   330→                protocol = session.get(Protocol, protocol_id)
   331→                if protocol:
   332→                    meta = protocol.metadata_ or {}
   333→                    protocol.metadata_ = {
   334→                        **meta,
   335→                        "pipeline_thread_id": thread_id,
   336→                    }
   337→                    session.add(protocol)
   338→                    session.commit()
   339→        except Exception:
   340→            logger.warning(
   341→                "Failed to store pipeline_thread_id for protocol %s",
   342→                protocol_id,
   343→            )
   344→
   345→        config = {"configurable": {"thread_id": thread_id}}
   346→
   347→        asyncio.run(_run_pipeline(initial_state, config, payload))
   348→
   349→        logger.info(
   350→            "Protocol pipeline completed for protocol %s",
   351→            protocol_id,
   352→        )
   353→
   354→    except Exception as e:
   355→        logger.exception(
   356→            "Protocol pipeline failed for protocol %s",
   357→            protocol_id,
   358→        )
   359→        reason = _categorize_pipeline_error(e)
   360→        # Auth expiry: do not retry; outbox marks dead_letter, UI shows login.
   361→        is_auth_expired = _is_auth_expired_error(e)
   362→        category = "auth_expired" if is_auth_expired else "pipeline_failed"
   363→        _update_protocol_failed(
   364→            protocol_id,
   365→            reason,
   366→            category,
   367→            type(e).__name__,
   368→        )
   369→        if is_auth_expired:
   370→            raise AuthExpiredError("Google credentials expired — sign in again") from e
   371→        raise
   372→
   373→
   374→async def retry_from_checkpoint(protocol_id: str) -> dict[str, Any]:
   375→    """Resume pipeline from last checkpoint for a failed protocol.
   376→
   377→    Passes None as the input state to graph.ainvoke, which tells LangGraph
   378→    to resume from the last saved checkpoint for the given thread_id instead
   379→    of starting from scratch. Reads thread_id from protocol.metadata_ where
   380→    it was stored during the original pipeline invocation.
   381→
   382→    Args:
   383→        protocol_id: Protocol ID — used to look up thread_id from metadata.
   384→
   385→    Returns:
   386→        Final pipeline state dict after resuming from checkpoint.
   387→    """
   388→    with Session(engine) as session:
   389→        protocol = session.get(Protocol, protocol_id)
   390→        if not protocol:
   391→            raise ValueError(f"Protocol {protocol_id} not found")
   392→        thread_id = (protocol.metadata_ or {}).get("pipeline_thread_id", protocol_id)
   393→
   394→    from protocol_processor.graph import get_graph
   395→
   396→    graph = await get_graph()
   397→    config = {"configurable": {"thread_id": thread_id}}
   398→    # Pass None as input — LangGraph resumes from last checkpoint
   399→    result = await graph.ainvoke(None, config)
   400→    return result
   401→
